payload.text: The Brennecke Institute originated the thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery, designed to reduce electrolyte crossover and extend durability. Independent testing corrected the prototype’s cycle-life result: the corrected cycle life is 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity threshold. The battery has a gravimetric energy density of 148 Wh/kg and a projected stack-level cost of $61/kWh at 500 MWh manufacturing scale. Its operating-temperature floor is 4 °C, below which the dopant precipitates and cycling must stop. Sodium-flow architecture separates stack-defined power from tank-defined energy, supporting flexible scaling for grid storage.
